audit_findings.title: GCU’s Title IV authorization had expired before the valuation date without a supplied resolution
audit_findings.magnitude: 89.4% of first-half 2026 service revenue, approximately $512.1 million computed from $572.805 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Loss or restriction of Title IV eligibility would reduce GCU enrollment and tuition-derived service revenue, lowering OE and sustainable growth.
audit_findings.evidence: Our primary university partner, GCU, currently operates under a provisional program participation agreement that expires on June 30, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: Expiration of the stated June 30, 2026 agreement is demonstrated, but loss of eligibility is not. Certification may be continuing month-to-month while ED reviews renewal; the supplied post-expiration 10-Q does not establish the actual status. Because GCU generated 89.4% of service revenue, an adverse resolution could change the valuation conclusion materially.
audit_findings.action: Obtain ED correspondence or a subsequent filing confirming whether GCU is fully, provisionally, or month-to-month certified and identifying all conditions, restrictions, financial protections, and duration; rerun OE and growth scenarios for any disclosed restrictions.

audit_findings.title: The overwhelmingly concentrated GCU earnings stream is now terminable
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed $20 million annual revenue reduction under the amended MSA, equal to 1.8% of 2025 service revenue; filed operating-income effect described as immaterial
audit_findings.mechanism: Contract termination or repricing would affect forecast OE and terminal value through GCU-derived service fees.
audit_findings.evidence: Furthermore, GCU has the right to terminate the Master Services Agreement after July 1, 2025 upon at least eighteen (18) months prior written notice, and, upon the termination or expiration of the Master Services Agreement, GCU is not required to continue using us as the provider of the services thereunder.
audit_findings.explanation: The supplied latest 10-Q resolves the stated termination finding: the July 29, 2026 amended MSA eliminated GCU’s termination-for-convenience right and extended the initial term through June 30, 2041. Concentration remains high at 89.4% of first-half 2026 revenue, but it no longer makes the earnings stream presently terminable on the cited terms. The disclosed economic revision reduces annual revenue by about 1.8% of 2025 revenue while management expects an immaterial operating-income decline because reimbursements also end.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the valuation’s normalized OE reflects the amended MSA’s net operating-income economics; rerun only if subsequent results show a material OE effect inconsistent with the filed immaterial-impact estimate.

audit_findings.title: The settlement add-back may misclassify recurring regulatory litigation as nonrecurring
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed $35.0 million settlement charge, equal to 15.0% of the $233.6 million anchor OE; further exposure unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back a charge that represents recurring regulatory or litigation costs raises normalized OE and every forecast and terminal-value cash flow; future judgments or settlements would also reduce equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company is a party to several matters alleging that, in the performance of its marketing services provided on behalf of GCU, it made false or misleading representations regarding the time to complete and the costs associated with and/or accreditation issues related to certain GCU graduate programs.
audit_findings.explanation: The $35 million settlement and its normalization are demonstrated, while recurrence and the amount of additional losses are unresolved. Multiple related cases remain active, including RICO and consumer-protection claims, with no accrued liability or estimable loss range. The normalized charge is large relative to anchor OE and therefore can change the valuation conclusion if any meaningful portion is recurring or followed by additional claims.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the exact after-tax settlement adjustment in 2025 OE; obtain claimed damages, class-certification status, legal-cost run rate, insurance and indemnification terms, reserves, and management’s loss-range analysis; rerun with the supportable recurring legal cost and probability-weighted claims.

audit_findings.title: Third-party-servicer status creates contingent claims beyond LOPE’s own recorded obligations
audit_findings.mechanism: Repayments, fines, sanctions, remediation costs, or lost servicing authority would reduce OE and cash in the equity bridge and could impair growth.
audit_findings.evidence: Be jointly and severally liable with the institution to the Secretary for any violation by the servicer of any statutory provision of or applicable to Title IV of the HEA, any regulatory provision prescribed under that statutory authority, and any applicable special arrangement, agreement, or limitation entered into under the authority of statutes applicable to Title IV of the HEA.
audit_findings.explanation: Joint-and-several liability is a demonstrated legal mechanism, but the record identifies no specific violation, assessment, reserve, or estimable exposure. It may affect value, particularly because GCE performs Title IV functions for its dominant partner, but the supplied evidence cannot establish present materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain third-party-servicer compliance audits, ED program-review findings and notices, return-to-Title-IV exceptions, indemnification and insurance coverage, and any post-filing assessments or reserves; rerun if those records identify a probable or reasonably estimable exposure.

audit_findings.title: July 2026 federal-aid changes may constitute a structural break absent from historical OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Loan limits and program-level eligibility tests may reduce enrollment, alter program mix, increase compliance costs, and lower forecast OE and growth relative to the historical trend.
audit_findings.evidence: OBBBA creates the “Do No Harm” accountability framework, effective July 2026, that institutions must satisfy at the program level in order for students to continue to receive Federal Direct Loans for such programs.
audit_findings.explanation: The statutory changes are effective and the filing identifies GCU’s Masters in Mental and Social Health programs as failing the indicated historical metric, but no filed revenue, contribution-profit, enrollment, or compliance-cost exposure is supplied. The risk is forward-looking and has not yet produced a demonstrated financial effect in the historical OE series.
audit_findings.action: Track final implementation guidance and obtain program-level revenue, contribution profit, enrollment, borrowing dependence, updated test results, planned closures or tuition changes, and post-July 2026 enrollment behavior; rerun growth and OE when measurable effects emerge.
